“We are designing systems that are both resilient and secure in order to protect our house.”

“We create an environment in which our métiers can innovate with confidence.”

United by a shared passion for innovation, our growing tech community works in a constantly evolving environment, using advanced tools and expressing their creativity to support the different professions, from the design of objects to their sale.

Through a series of 13 episodes, Hermès employees share their experiences and invite you to discover their daily lives in the house. 

In this episode, discover the role of our managers in Hermès stores through the stories of Eleonora, Hugo, Jackie, and Jihye.

“What I like the most in my day-to-day life is the sense of community and collective spirit I have with my teams.”

“As a manager twice a year, we have the opportunity to choose and purchase the products we will have in our store.”

In an inspiring multicultural environment, our store and department managers play a strategic role, building bespoke career paths while benefiting from a wide range of training and development programmes that support continuous learning.

title: Women's fall-winter 2026, the second chapter

description:
On a June evening in Los Angeles, Hermès unveils the second chapter of its fall-winter 2026 collection.

At sunset, a pavilion in Los Angeles transforms into a luminous stage. Dressmaking and dance converge through gestures perfected over time.​

Tailoring contrasts with gathered, draped, and fluid constructions, expressing multiple facets of femininity through a dialogue between structure and flou, tension and release.​
A silhouette in transformation. Silk, satin, and velvet bring lightness, movement, and grace, ​contrasted with the sleek precision of leather, while midnight hues intensify vivid jewel tones.​
At golden hour, the atmospheric setting is suffused with neon-lit jaune flave, dissolving the boundary between stage and landscape. Against this panoramic backdrop, silhouettes hover between rehearsal and performance, reality and reverie.​

title: Paste forward 🎲🐴

description:
An ode to the delicacy of a colorful, singular marine world.

To design the motifs on the Natures Marines collection’s 34 pieces, Charlotte Macaux Perelman and Alexis Fabry, artisti directors of the Hermès home universe, called upon illustrator Katie Scott. Inspired by nineteenth-century English botanical illustrations and the marine flora of the Welsh coastline, the British artist meticulously drew the hundred plant species that adorn the porcelain, playing with a palette of thirty vibrant tones: cool greens, mineral beiges, deep oranges and reds.

Discover more at h.fr/NaturesMarines

In the courtyard of the Naples State Archives, a series of frescoes depicting the life of Saint Benedict, a jewel of 16th century Italian art, have regained their original vibrancy and splendor thanks to expert restorers. 

Since 2021, Hermès, which celebrates drawing in its creations, has been supporting the preservation of artisanal fresco know-how and the restoration of works visible in the public space all over the Italian peninsula, thus helping to preserve the country’s cultural heritage.

description:
Discover Barénia Eau de Parfum Intense: more powerful. More mysterious. A new, more intense Barénia that reveals a profound sensuality and highlights a new facet of the Hermès chypre.

“Artisans say Barénia leather returns your caress, and that's the sensation I sought to capture with Barénia Eau de Parfum Intense. Barénia leather moves beyond the realm of metaphor: its presence becomes physical, almost tactile.” - Christine Nagel, Hermès perfumer. 

For this olfactory variant, Hermès perfumer Christine Nagel has explored the composition of the original Barénia in greater depth. The patchouli is denser, the oakwood more enveloping. Leathery notes complete a palette created with butterfly lily and miracle berry at its heart. Together, they make up the signature of an intense, enigmatic femininity.

description:
The steady roar of the ocean, the sound of silk as it catches the breeze since 1937... 🌊 Here, a moment of calm with the Bouquets Sellier carré, designed by Pierre Marie Studio and captured by Sarah Blais.

The story behind: Straps, curb chains, harnesses and stirrups are gathered into bright bouquets, like cut flowers. Horses' heads, their manes rippling, burst from the sheaves like wild blooms. Arranged on graphic horse blankets, folded to show their front and reverse sides, the four compositions are a perfect metamorphosis of fabrics, leather and metal parts. The illusion is complete.

title: Close your eyes and listen...

description:
Since 1937, the Hermès carré, first imagined by Robert Dumas, keeps on swinging. Discover this harmony of Grand Tralala carrés, designed by Virginie Jamin, captured by Sarah Blais.

The story behind: In the 19th century, the steeds of the Hungarian Royal Guard sported a ceremonial harness with gleaming buckles, like this framed bridle with its delicate leather straps. Beneath bands of gradient colors, Virginie Jamin's delicate lines are endlessly intensified and repeated, giving this emblematic equestrian motif a new rainbow.

description:
Discover our new collections for the home presented at Milan Design Week. 

The new creations can be discovered in white – nearly colorless – suspended boxes, projecting halos of bright colors onto the floor. 

It is through the immateriality of their aura that the objects first appear, like emotions. This staging is a quest for the object, for the luminous vibration that makes it familiar. 

The creations appear gradually in glimpses and reflections. Colors and transparency vary according to the technique used, making each piece unique. 

Blowing glass, casing, layering and fusing it… The object transforms the space with its light, making the room feel alive. Certain objects, furniture, and fabrics shimmer, vibrating with a familiar halo.

description:
Hermès reinvents time at Watches and Wonders Geneva 2025.

Philippe Delhotal, Creative Director of Hermès Watchmaking, unveils the Maillon Libre collection, a bold reinterpretation of the iconic anchor chain link as a wristwatch and a brooch watch. 

The enigmatic and singular wristwatch appeals with its complex structure. Meanwhile, the discreet, almost imperceptible display of time incorporated into the bracelet design adds a playful and surprising touch.

The brooch watch, one of the most ancient masculine accessories and the ultimate nomadic object, can be worn on its own or transformed into a pendant.

Maillon libre is an expressive and precious collection where elegance aligns with the pace of a time imbued with astonishment.

title: The Making of the Hermès Maillon Libre collection

description:
Hermès reinvents time at Watches and Wonders Geneva 2025, with its signature complication "Le temps suspendu".

A dialogue with Philippe Delhotal, creative director of Hermès Watchmaking, reveals how this complication captures the essence of Hermès' approach to time.

Time as a friend, this time that is so dear to the house, extends an invitation to break free from temporal constraints and seize the moment.

Launched in 2011, "Le temps suspendu" is a playful expression of Hermès time. It is the embodiment of time as a friend, toying with conventions to better celebrate the present moment. In 2025, Hermès has redesigned this singular complication on the Arceau and for the first time, offers this function in the Hermès Cut collection.

Discover the Trait d’Hermès Lip Pencils. ​ 

Thanks to the precision pencil tip, application is easy and controlled, creating an even line. The intense color glides on effortlessly to outline, define and enhance the contours of the lips or color them naturally. The pencils can also be used for touch-ups, to prevent lipstick from bleeding, or to prolong its hold throughout the day. They can soften or, conversely, accentuate the look of a lipstick. Their matte finish interacts naturally with the different finishes of Rouge Hermès lipsticks, whose shades they complement perfectly. Make-up becomes free and inventive again, and as intuitive as child’s play. ​

Sixteen shades, from Rouge Érable to Beige Thé, embody all the color families (red, pink, orange and beige) and mirror the signature shades of Rouge Hermès lipsticks: Rouge H, Rouge Casaque, Orange Boîte, and more. ​

title: The Hermès Beauty Gestures by Gregoris Pyrpylis – Trait d’Hermès  Lip Pencils

description:
Discover the Trait d’Hermès Eye Pencils. ​ 

Water-resistant and suitable for sensitive eyes, the formula's rich, creamy texture delivers a non-greasy finish for an even, buildable line. The firm but silky-soft tip is perfect for creating either lines or blocks of color. And to vary the make-up effects, the pencils come in two finishes – matte or iridescent – depending on the shade. ​

The color is simple to apply, using either a brush or the built-in smudger to define, accentuate, open up and intensify the gaze. The line can be fine and precise or more emphatic, for graphic or blended results ranging from the ultra-natural to the ultra-sophisticated. Combining the functions of kohl and eyeliner, the pencils can also be used to highlight the lower lid or waterline. A reinvention of the gaze with a simple line. ​

There are twenty-four pencils – the house’s lucky number. ​

description:
Discover the Trait d’Hermès Eyeliner. ​

This new refillable object designed by Pierre Hardy combines elegance with function. In many respects, the tube and metal cap recall the cartridge fountain pens used in childhood. The soft bristles of the tip, which do not dry out over time, form a brush point for drawing a precise and buildable line – whether using the slender side for an ultra-fine result, or the flat side to create the thickest of looks. ​

The water-resistant, quick-drying and long-wear formula is made with 63% ingredients of natural origin. In a single stroke, the fluid texture delivers a clean, even line with a uniform, satiny finish. ​

The Encre Noire shade is as unique as the object itself. This highly pigmented black becomes a line and a color. ​

description:
Discover the inspiration behind Barénia, the new women's fragrance created by Christine Nagel, the house's perfumer.

Composed of limpid curves hallmarked with a metal plate of Clou Médor studs, this object is the ultimate twist on the Hermès Collier de chien bracelet. Settling on the skin, it becomes a fragrance.

Designer Philippe Mouquet, a longstanding partner of the house, drew inspiration from the iconic Collier de chien bracelet to create a bottle of crystal-clear curves and
precious metal. Its elliptical shape, overlaid with a metal plate bearing four contoured studs with domed facets, echoes the line of the bracelet.

These heritage codes come together harmoniously to create a powerful piece symbolic of a lifelong signature fragrance.

Discover how artists and technicians joined forces for On The Wings of Hermès, a project that echoes the know-how and artisan spirit of Hermès. 

On the Wings of Hermès, a film by Hermès and director Jaco Van Dormael takes the viewers on a journey into the story of Pegasus, the winged horse from Greek mythology, through a mischievously captivating tale divided into six acts.  
 
Each scene features one of Pegasus' foals discovering a form of lightness and learning how to fly, recounted by a narrator with a mellow, rich voice. 
 
These sketches are brought to life by delicate ballets of hand expressions and passionate bodies. Dancers, acrobats, and actors evolve in the scenery, as if in a dream.

title: Behind the scenes of On The Wings of Hermès

description:
A Cinematic Journey Behind the Scenes of a Dream. 

In this 35-minutes film, where magic inhabits every scene, Hermès and director Jaco Van Dormael reimagined the story of Pegasus, the winged horse from Greek mythology, through a mischievously captivating tale divided into six acts. 

Each scene features one of Pegasus' foals discovering a form of lightness and learning how to fly, recounted by a narrator with a mellow, rich voice. 

These sketches are brought to life by delicate ballets of hand expressions and passionate bodies. Dancers, acrobats, and actors evolve in the scenery, as if in a dream. 
This film combines the art of dance with object theatre, and life-size gestures with miniature accessories. Playing with scale, extended metaphors give free rein to the imagination. 

Experimental art blends with cinematic spectacle in its naive and quirky use of special effects. Handcrafted tricks and artisanal stage sets echo the know-how and gestural culture of Hermès. 

A tale in movement full of emotion.

description:
Amidst the quiet streets and stone dwellings of Villaines-les-Rochers, an ancient troglodyte village in France, lies a tradition of wickerwork. Skilled hands meticulously weave together slender withies of the petite grisette willow, transforming them into works of art. 

The art of wickerwork has been practised since the 7th century in Villaines-les-Rochers, and is perpetuated by the fifty or so wickerworkers and basket-makers in the local wickerwork cooperative established in 1849. 

Hermès, which has been partner of this structure for over forty years, has strengthened its commitment over time, in a spirit of constantly renewed creativity. From household objects, the collaboration has extended to incorporate bags and fashion accessories, fostering a culture of innovation and creativity.

By promoting these exceptional skills, new vocations are inspired and the craft lives on.  

#HermesFootsteps​

description:

description:
H24 Herbes Vives invites us to follow in the footsteps of the contemporary man in motion who is at home in urban nature. His senses are heightened, his view of the world sharper. 

“I was inspired by the happy smell of nature after the rain. That unique moment when nature and the city, still drenched with water, release new scents and take on new colours.” 
Christine Nagel, Hermès perfumer.

Refillable and fashioned from light, the H24 Herbes Vives bottle is the sensitive symbol of another kind of masculinity. Light shines through the glass, as if diffused by the leaves of trees after the rain.

title: Saut Hermès 2024 l Free your mind

description:
The Saut Hermès returns to Paris on 15th, 16th, 17th March 2024.
The fourteenth edition of the Saut Hermès will take place for the third time in the Grand Palais Éphémère located in the heart of Paris.
Reserved for the global show-jumping elite and rising stars under the age of 25, this competition also celebrates the equestrian world with a series of unique experiences.

Inside the Grand Palais Éphémère, visitors can wander around the stands, cheer on the competitors and watch the equestrian show like no other!

Outside, the stables adjoin a paddock where riders and their mounts can rest and relax.

On the other side of the central aisle is a manege for equestrian activities and other events, open to all passers-by!

This year, the Saut Hermès returns to the heart of the French capital to delight riders and non-riders of all ages once again.

title: Behind the saddle with Astier Nicolas, Hermès partner rider

description:
It's time for a joyful show!

24 Faubourg is sleeping, leaving the window displays to their nocturnal calm as snow falls outside. And yet, behind this frosty scene, they light up, revealing their mysteries to passers-by. Pegasus strikes the ground with his leather hoof, snorts and sets off. The show can begin.

Pegasus challenges the camels to a race to 24 Faubourg. They are running and flying when a Constance bag falls into step. Grand Jeté and Farandole scarf rings appear in the sky. Is it a mirage? Or the competition trophy? Pegasus leaps into the air to get closer to them.

His momentum is so strong that Pegasus is propelled into space! In a risky jump, he manages to slide over a silky Milky Way to planet Clic H. He wants to remove its rings and attach them to his hooves. But a stellar breeze takes him to a large starry door: Pegasus finds himself in front of 24 Faubourg! 

Discover more on: https://h.fr/Holidays2023

title: The Hermès Parfums-Jardins collection

description:
Park Myung Bae creates traditional furniture in wood that he allows to rest for seven years before crafting it. ​

Sohn Dae Hyun applies the ancient art of lacquering to a diverse range of materials.​

Park Moon Yeol chisels ornamentation into metal pieces such as locks and padlocks. Park Sung Kyu participates to the conservation of the leather lacquering technique. ​

These artisans, all custodians of the excellence of contemporary Korean craftsmanship, were chosen to rekindle know-how that existed under the Joseon dynasty (1392-1897). ​

Arumjigi Culture Keepers Foundation, whose mission is to preserve and support traditional Korean culture, entrusted them with the painstaking task of recreating objects that furnished the palaces of Seoul. ​

A long and meticulous period of research in museums, seeking out treasures from the past and forgotten techniques, allowed them to reproduce copies of these precious repositories of Korean culture. ​

title: Astonishing orange | Hermès

description:
In this 1st episode, embark on a journey through creativity with Daichiro Shinjo.​

Calligrapher Daichiro Shinjo, who continues to bring new light to traditional calligraphy, travels to Miyako Island in Okinawa Prefecture, his hometown and current base of activities. There, he meets a female dyeing artist who, with the traditional craft of hemp fabric called Miyako jofu, which boasts over 400 years of history, faces anew this place where indigo dyeing has been popular for a long time.She grows her own Indian indigo and uses it as a dye for her creations. ​

Daichiro Shinjo | Calligrapher ​
Born in Miyako Island, Okinawa, in 1992. He began calligraphy in his childhood when he was familiar with Zen and Buddhist culture. Now he is bringing a new light to calligraphy with an unconventional style against the backdrop of Okinawan spiritual culture. He also participated in "UNTITLED, ART" (San Francisco) and is active internationally.​

"HUMAN ODYSSEY" is a documentary film series in which creators who passionately pursue creation embark on a journey to discover craftsmanship. Calligrapher Daichiro Shinjo, architect Tsuyoshi Tane, roboticist Tomotaka Takahashi, photographer Kazuhei Kimura, chef Kotaro Meguro, and ceramic artist Raku Kichizaemon XVI. In this 6th episode, embark on a journey through creativity with Raku Kichizaemon XVI.​

The Raku Family is a prestigious ceramic art family loved by Sen no Rikyu, the great master of the Japanese tea ceremony. As a young leader of a Kyoto-based long-established business with a history of more than 450 years, Raku Kichizaemon XVI, seeking a balance between tradition and innovation, visits the Hermès studio in France. He meets Jérôme Giboire, a veteran artisan sellier for many years, and Romain Haye, an artisan sellier-maroquinier of the same generation, who share their delicate handiwork, and they exchange words about their craftsmanship. ​

Raku Kichizaemon XVI | Ceramic artist ​
Born in 1981 in Kyoto. He is the eldest son of Raku Kichizaemon XV of the Raku Family, which began in the Azuchi-Momoyama period and continued for 450 years. After graduating from Tokyo Zokei University with a degree in sculpture, he studied in London. He returned to Japan and has worked as a ceramic artist for the Raku Family since 2011. In July 2019, he took the name of Raku Kichizaemon XVI. While keeping his focus on tradition, he is also making tea bowls that are in line with modern life. ​

description:
Discover Hermès know-how through a series of colorful videos. 

MODELER: Creating an accurate pattern is the starting point for every tailored Hermès garment. 

After listening to the customer's wishes, the tailor takes measurements, then models the construction base of the piece according to the client’s unique form, tracing the pattern on paper before cutting it, then making it in the chosen fabric. 

After developing this pattern, the tailor "detaches" the piece, that is, they cut the various sections of the pattern into the actual fabric, taking care to join up each line of the design. 

They then assemble the garment, conduct successive fittings, and make final adjustments so that the piece meets both the customer's expectations and Hermès' quality criteria.

description:
Discover the Hermès home collections unveiled at the Milan Design Week. 

For the first time, textiles have become the central theme of a home collection. 

They express lightness with a collection of blankets whose designs are the starting point for exploring new know-how. 

Five cashmere creations form the basis of this manifesto for lightness. With its colored panels assembled by linking, the Construction blanket resembles a stained-glass window in textile. 

The Surface bedspread features surprising hexagons crafted in cashmere and combines the meticulous techniques of patchwork and quilting. 

H Pythagore plays with the assembly of hand-woven and hand-dyed colored squares. The geometric patterns of H Tartan and H Tissage are a reminder that lightness cannot exist without structure.

Discover how to apply your Rose Hermès Silky Blush and your Rose Hermès Rosy lip enhancer. 

The Silky Blush has a semi-matte finish, embossed with texture resembling silk twill. A fine, silky, long-lasting powder for a luminous, radiant complexion. The Rosy lip enhancer reveals the lips' natural beauty. With its fine and delicate waxy finish, the Rosy lip enhancer melts over the lip, leaving a hint of transparent pink and a matt luminosity. 

Lips are delicately smoothed with a soft-focus effect. Rose Hermès Silky Blush and Rose Hermès rosy lip enhancer are refillable beauty objects made to last. 

The collection Rose Hermès is composed of eight shades of Rose Hermès Silky Blush, two blush brushes and three Rosy lip enhancers.

CUISINER: To make colors according to recipes prescribed by our colorists, the artisans still largely work by hand.

description:

COUPER: After creating the pattern for a garment, the tailor “detaches” it by cutting the various parts of the pattern from the fabric, taking care to connect each line of the design. 

They then assemble the garment, conduct fitting sessions, and make the final adjustments, so that the piece satisfies the customer’s expectations and Hermès’ quality standards.

description:
Hermès trains new generations of artisans from all backgrounds for its leather métiers, strengthening the multiplicity and diversity of its leather workshops. 

Florists, jewellers, butchers, young graduates, job seekers, etc.: the identity and experience of those who join the Hermès leatherworking schools is not important. First and foremost, training coordinators like Gabrielle and Christophe build on the dexterity and capacity for learning of these students with unusual career paths, who are recruited through the Pôle Emploi agencies in the regions in which the French manufacturing facilities are established. 

Acquiring the know-how and qualities of a Hermès artisan – meticulousness, precision, attention to quality, perseverance, etc. – goes far beyond a simple exercise. Behind the gesture, a posture and an attitude give the work meaning and constitute a promise of pride for the future artisans.

title: Reinvent our métiers | Hermès

description:
Through a series of 11 episodes, Hermès employees share their voices, inviting you into the heart of their daily lives in the house.

In this episode, discover Manuela’s career path, who is currently the director of the Hermès workshops in Paris. 

During her 26 years at Hermès, Manuela has had a career path that has allowed her to satisfy her taste for bold bets. She has experienced mobility and different positions and countries, from Pantin to Munich, from Los Angeles to Tokyo. 

Hired as a leather goods craftsperson at the age of 23, she shows that there is no set path in the house, but rather a series of diverse encounters and opportunities that are seized as projects and activities develop: “Hermès gave me a chance, even though I didn’t tick all the boxes. From leather-worker to workshop manager, this bespoke career path has helped me forge very strong bonds of trust with the teams.”

As an architect, Claudine has for a long time supervised the Hermès workshop construction sites, always keeping in mind sustainability and consideration for networks of local partners working in construction. 

The objective is to achieve more ambitious goals than the existing standards, sustainable construction reflects Hermès' commitment to reducing carbon emissions, improving air quality, sourcing locally and respecting biodiversity and environmental quality.

description:
These classes of 14 and 15-year-olds in the Île-de-France region, at the Michelet professional high school in Saint-Ouen, and Staël high school in the 15th arrondissement of Paris, have neither maths nor French lessons today. 

Benjamin, Emmanuelle and Diane, saddler-leatherworkers, have come to their classrooms to convey “the pleasure of doing and sharing”. By meeting these craftsmen, who share their passion with students as part of the Manufacto programme initiated by the Fondation d’Entreprise Hermès, a new lesson was learned: that you can make your life by making objects.

description:
Pushing open the door of one of Hermès’ fifteen repair workshops around the world is like entering a magicians’ den, where the passage of time is made to disappear. 

In Hong Kong, on the 22nd floor of a tower in the Admiralty district where they have laid out their tools, Christelle, Farid and Alexandre save their best tricks for objects that have a past. Unseen and unnoticed, these experienced artisans, trained in French leather goods workshops, make a well-loved bag look new again, by changing a handle, retouching an area of color or using the saddle stitch. 

Restoring, repairing, it’s what their “metier” is all about.

Hundreds of inhabitants of Sorède, in the south of France, braided whips and riding crops in hackberry wood until the car and the tractor supplanted the horse.

description:
Droplets, waves and mountains… the etchings held prisoner in blocks of stone were the inspiration for the Japanese master bookbinders’ marbled paper.

Inkjet printing has transposed these effects to fabric, without ever equalling the delicacy and radiance of the patterns found by Hermès in an old album in the archives of its Lyon textile sector. 

After years of research, this technique of silk marbling using a compressed, through-colored starch paste was rediscovered in Kyoto. The Nose family is its custodian.

Directed by Frédéric Laffont.

In Kongoussi in Burkina Faso, the Tiipaalga association teaches women how to build these fuel-efficient wood-burning stoves, which are less polluting and improve living conditions.

This is just one idea amongst many initiatives supported locally by Hermès through the Livelihoods fund.
